spans.s:
r. 1st cl. (भिक्षते)
1 To beg.
2 To obtain.
3 To fail of obtaining.
4 To solicit any thing through cupidity or covetousness.
5 To be weary or distressed.

Service.
2

Hire, wages.
3 Begging, asking.
4 The thing obtained by begging, alms.
5 A mouthful or handful of food, given as alms.
E.
भिक्ष to beg or obtain by begging, अङ् and टाप् aff.

n. (-णं)
Begging, asking alms.
E.
भिक्ष to beg, ल्युट् aff.

mfn. (-णः-णा-णं)
Asking, begging.
E.
भिक्ष to beg, शानच् aff.

mf. (-कः-की)
A mendicant, a beggar.
E.
भिक्षा alms, and काकन् aff.

mf. (-रः-री)
A mendicant, a beggar.
E.
भिक्षा alms, चर to go, aff. ट.

n. (-नं)
Begging, mendicancy.
E.
भिक्षा alms, and अटन going about for.

n. (-न्नं)
Food obtained as alms.
E.
भिक्षा, and अन्न food.

n. (-त्रं)
A beggar's bowl, a vessel for collecting alms.
E.
भिक्षा, and पात्र a vessel.

n. (-त्वं)
1 Profligacy, roguery.
2 Mendicancy, subsisting on alms.
E.
भिक्षाशिन् a beggar, त्व abstract aff.

mfn. (-शी-शिनी-शि)
1 A beggar, a mendicant, subsisting on alms.
2 Dishonest.
E.
भिक्षा alms, अश to eat, aff. णिनि.

mfn. (-र्हः-र्हा-र्हं)
Fit for a beggar.
E.
भिक्षा, and अर्ह fit for.

mfn. (-तः-ता-तं)
Begged, sought as alms.
E.
भिक्ष to beg, क्त aff.

m. (-क्षुः)
1 The mendicant; the Hindu who has entered the fourth order, and subsists wholly upon alms.
2 The fourth order of the

Hindus.
3

A Bauddha mendicant.
E.
भिक्ष to beg, aff. उ.

mf. (-कः-की)
A beggar.
E.
भिक्षु a beggar, कन् added.

f. (-टी)
Old or ragged raiment, the garb of a beggar.
E.
भिक्षु a beggar, सम् with, घट to endeavour, aff. अण् and ङीप्.

m. (-रः)
Scattering alms.
E.
भिक्षा alms, उत् before कॄ to scatter, aff. अप्.
